companyDescription: AI-driven drug discovery (TechBio) · REC-4881 in FDA registrational-pathway discussions for familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) · partnered with Sanofi/Roche/Genentech ($500M+ milestones delivered) · Tempus AI data-licensing partner
priceNote: Prior same-day draft used $3.19 — live price $3.87 is +21.3% higher. The move traces to a real, dated catalyst the draft missed: on Sep 21, 2026, Recursion extended its Tempus AI data-licensing deal through Nov 2029 and granted Tempus a license to its TxFM RNA-sequencing foundation model, restructuring fees from a discretionary ~$84M ceiling to a committed $42M over 3 years — a durable, non-dilutive revenue signal the market rewarded with a same-day +3.92% pop and has kept building on since.
summary: Two things changed since the last snapshot: the Tempus AI partnership was extended and restructured (Sep 21, 2026) into committed, non-dilutive payments, and the REC-4881 FDA registrational-pathway update for familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) remains the live near-term catalyst, now dated precisely to Oct 15, 2026 (previously badged inconsistently as 'H2 2026' against the same catalystDate — fixed in this refresh). Consensus (7 analysts, S&P Global) $7.22 implies +86.6% upside from $3.87, though Morgan Stanley's prior trim to $5.30 (Equal Weight) remains a real caution flag from a named, conservative voice. Base case (+35%) sits above the core lane's realized 14d P75 of +6.6% — the gap reflects the multi-month horizon to a registrational-pathway resolution, not near-term optimism bias.

catalysts.name: REC-4881 FDA Registrational Pathway Update
catalysts.description: Update on the registrational pathway discussions for REC-4881 in familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP), an AI-discovered asset partnered with Sanofi/Roche. Targeted for Oct 15, 2026.

risks: Morgan Stanley's target trim to $5.30 (Equal Weight) from $5.50 remains the most recent named-analyst caution signal — no new upgrade has offset it since
Target dispersion remains wide ($4.00 low to $10 high) — genuine methodology disagreement on how to value the TechBio platform

Still unprofitable with cash-burn risk — a hawkish Fed (rates hiked to 3.75-4.00%) raises the cost of any future capital raise, though the Tempus restructuring reduces near-term revenue uncertainty somewhat
A 'registrational pathway update' is a process milestone, not a binary approval/rejection — the market reaction could be muted if it's just incremental clarity rather than a clear green light
The stock has already run +21% into this refresh on the Tempus news — some of the near-term goodwill may be pulled forward ahead of the Oct 15 pathway update itself

estimateDates.note: Extended through Nov 2029; restructured to $42M committed over 3 years + TxFM model license
Now matches catalystDate — prior draft had this fuzzily badged as 'H2 2026'

analystTargets.note: Trimmed from $5.50 — most recent named caution flag

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16, 2026 (first hike since 2023); next FOMC Oct 27-28, 2026 — after the Oct 15 pathway update, so it shouldn't collide directly, but tightens the backdrop for any future raise.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Inflation-driven hike; RXRX is still unprofitable and cash-burning, making it directly exposed to higher financing costs, though the Tempus restructuring adds committed near-term revenue.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: TechBio/AI-drug-discovery names with negative FCF are among the most rate-sensitive cohorts — a hawkish Fed compounds an already-cautious Morgan Stanley call.
macroRisk.summary: HIGH macro risk — the renewed hiking cycle directly raises RXRX's future financing costs, though the newly-committed Tempus payments partially de-risk near-term cash needs.

Morgan Stanley's target trim is still a real caution flag worth respecting even as the Tempus restructuring adds genuine near-term revenue visibility — size for two-sided risk, not just the headline R/R.
